ULM / MLM activity scores (decoupler-style)

calc_lm_activity.Rd

Rust implementation of decoupler's univariate (ULM) and multivariate (MLM) linear model activity scores. Per observation, the observed values of the features are regressed on the weights of each source's targets (ULM: one model per source; MLM: all sources in one model), and the t-value (or the coefficient) of the slope is the activity. Positive means the targets move in the direction of their weights.

Behaviour worth knowing:

  • Rows with non-finite values are dropped (with a warning) before scoring.

  • Constant observations score 0 with a p-value of 1.

  • MLM errors on collinear sources (duplicated or proportional target sets, or a set covering every feature with one weight).

  • The p-values treat the features as independent.

  • fdr is the Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment per observation across sources, decoupler's scheme. decoupler only adjusts ULM; here both methods get it, so compare pvals against decoupler's MLM output.

Usage

calc_lm_activity(mat, net, lm_params = params_lm_activity())

Arguments

mat

Numerical matrix of features x samples with row names, or a named numeric vector (e.g., a contrast's t statistics), treated as one sample. Should be roughly normal: normalised and log-transformed counts, or contrast-level statistics.

net

data.frame. The network in long format with the columns source, target and optionally weight (decoupler / CollecTRI layout). Absent weights are set to 1.

lm_params

List. The parameters, see params_lm_activity(). This function generates a list containing:

  • method - String. "ulm" or "mlm".

  • stat - String. "t" or "coef".

  • p_values - Boolean. Shall p-values be computed.

  • tmin - Integer. Minimum number of targets per source in the data.

Value

For a matrix input, a list with the following elements:

  • es - Numerical matrix of samples x sources with the activities.

  • pvals - Numerical matrix of samples x sources with the two-sided p-values, or NULL if p_values = FALSE.

  • fdr - Numerical matrix of the BH-adjusted p-values (per sample across sources), or NULL if p_values = FALSE.

For a vector input, a data.table with the columns source, es, and, if requested, pvals and fdr. NULL with a warning if no source has at least tmin targets in the data.

References

Badia-i-Mompel, et al., Bioinform. Adv., 2022

Examples

# two regulators, one with its targets shifted up in the second sample
set.seed(42L)
genes <- sprintf("gene_%03i", 1:200)
mat <- matrix(
  rnorm(400),
  ncol = 2L,
  dimnames = list(genes, c("ctrl", "treated"))
)
mat[1:15, "treated"] <- mat[1:15, "treated"] + 2
net <- data.frame(
  source = rep(c("tf_a", "tf_b"), each = 15L),
  target = genes[c(1:15, 101:115)],
  weight = 1
)
res <- calc_lm_activity(
  mat,
  net,
  lm_params = params_lm_activity(p_values = TRUE)
)
res$es
#>             tf_a        tf_b
#> ctrl    2.133174  0.03763638
#> treated 7.184559 -0.70848693
